summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia and tracheostomy was admitted for chills, increased dyspnea, and dark green, blood-tinged sputum from her tracheostomy. She had recently been treated for Staphylococcus lugdunensis bacteremia and was on home vancomycin. Evaluation revealed no acute findings on chest X-ray, and ENT found no tracheal inflammation or purulence. Sputum culture grew MRSA, prompting a 5-day course of IV vancomycin at 1000 mg every 12 hours, up from her prior dose due to a low trough. She also received a unit of packed red blood cells for acute on chronic iron deficiency anemia, with hemoglobin improving from 6.8 to 8.2 g/dL. Hemoglobin electrophoresis was pending at discharge. She improved clinically, with resolution of chills and decreased secretions, and was discharged home to complete antibiotics with home health support.
